body: To clarify the use case, suppose you have a typical registration form with a checkbox at the end saying something like "I accept the Terms & Conditions". How do you ensure the checkbox must be ticked if not by declaring it as required?

Yeh, this looks like a valid bug. 

There are 2 ways of fixing it I can think of:
- quick & dirty: make the `CheckboxControlValueAccessor` write `null` instead of `false` when unchecked - not ideal as it is going to change model value assigned 
- have a separate `RequiredValidator` for checkboxes (we should probably also think of radios)

@kara I can PR this one if you could confirm that a checkbox-specific `RequiredValidator` is the way to go.
The "quick & dirty" fix wouldn't work if the model itself is initialised to `false` I guess? I.e. this case: http://plnkr.co/edit/fHpNhAQD2ZUvq5xpYL3R?p=preview

Hi, I just ran into the same issue and was wondering if a fix has been pushed. 

Thanks!
@pkozlowski-opensource  The second solution with the validator seems reasonable if you have time to take it on.

body:
Further updates for this bug.

@mirkonasato the reason why this is happening is because after you uncheck a checkbox that is checked when assigned with ngModel it does not change the value. So initially you'll start with undefined, then move to true after being checked, then it will stay true after being unchecked. Additionally, if the value is false in the model ngModel will not change the value at all when it is checked.

Additionally, as of `2.1.0` any checkbox in a form with a value of false, even if it's not required, renders the entire form invalid.

To get proper checkbox functionality you must remove it from your formgroup, and use the following code:

html:

```
<input type="checkbox"  id="my-check"  (change)="onChange($event)" [checked]="checkModel" />
<label for="my-check">Is Checked?</label>
```

ts:

```
onChange($event) {
  this.checkModel = $event.target.checked;
}
```

The desired behavior is that ngModel should handle this by sending either a true/false value to the model, and then a form should only accept a true/false value to be valid.
hi, which version will provide this fix ?

## I'm submitting a ... 

[ ] Regression (behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[x] Bug report 
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
## Current behavior Some months ago an issue related to required checkbox validation had been fixed and it now works as expected. See here: #11459 Unfortunately, the issue still occurs when placing the checkbox input within a custom component. **Form template:** ```
// variable 'checkboxValue: boolean' comes from controller // --> always ng-valid
Output: {{myForm.valid}} // BAD: output always true ``` **Component:** ``` @Component({ selector: "my-checkbox", template: '', providers: [ { provide: NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR, useExisting: forwardRef(() => MyCheckbox), multi: true } ] }) export class MyCheckbox implements ControlValueAccessor { @Input("name") name: string; @Input("required") required: boolean; private _innerValue: any; onChangeCallback: any = (_: any) => {}; onTouchedCallback: any = () => {}; get value(): any { return this._innerValue; }; set value(value: any) { if (value !== this._innerValue) { this._innerValue = value; this.onChangeCallback(value); } } writeValue(value: any): void { if (value !== this._innerValue) { this._innerValue = value; } } registerOnChange(fn: (_: any) => {}): void { this.onChangeCallback = fn; } registerOnTouched(fn: () => {}): void { this.onTouchedCallback = fn; } } ``` In that case, the validation state is NOT propagated properly to the host component. Thus, the enclosing form always remains valid even if unchecking the required checkbox. Like with the older issue, only setting ngModel to NULL would trigger correct propagation (not a desired approach). ## Expected behavior A required checkbox validation state (ng-valid, ng-invalid) should be propagated properly to the host component. Unchecking the inner checkbox (then ngModel == false) makes host component and form invalid. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? Unchecking a required checkbox within a custom component should prevent the form submission. ## Please tell us about your environment Angular version: 4.1.0 Browser: [all] Language: [all]
